business_summary: Action Construction Equipment operates in the construction equipment sector. In FY26 it earned a net profit of Rs 415 crore on a 15.4% operating margin, with no borrowings. Revenue has compounded at about 15% a year over three years and about 22% over five.
why_own: The case rests on sustained double-digit revenue growth, a wider operating margin (up 5.1 points in three years) and high returns on capital (ROCE 28.7%) with no debt, and cash flow matches profit. The stock trades at 28.7x trailing earnings, near its own 5-year median, so the price already assumes this record continues. Only financial metrics were supplied, with no results releases or call transcripts, so every driver here is a metric driver.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 14.95%).
The operating margin holds most of its gain (currently 15.36%, up 5.13 points over three years).
Returns on capital stay high (ROCE currently 28.67%, ROE 22.9%).
Reported profit converts into operating cash (cash flow / profit currently 1.01x).

kill_criteria.description: ROCE falls below 15%, meaning returns on capital have lost much of their current level.
Operating margin falls below 10%, giving back most of the three-year gain.

risks.statement: Valuation is demanding: 28.7x trailing earnings and 6.23x book, so a slowdown in growth or margin could be punished. The P/E is only about 1.8% above its 5-year year-end median.
Growth is slowing on the numbers: the 3-year revenue CAGR (14.95%) is below the 5-year CAGR (21.73%). The reason is untested with the evidence provided.
The margin gain of 5.13 points over three years may not hold. Why the margin rose is untested with the evidence provided, so it could partly reverse.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis leans on a margin gain and growth rate that the evidence never explains. Profit compounded 34.24% a year against revenue at 14.95%, so most earnings growth came from margin expansion. Revenue growth is also slowing, from 21.73% over five years to 14.95% over three. At 28.7x earnings and 6.23x book, the price assumes both continue. The thesis is wrong if the margin drifts back toward its starting level of about 10.2% (15.36 minus 5.13), leaving earnings growth at the revenue pace. The kill threshold on margin (10%) sits below that starting level, so it only trips after the whole gain is gone. What would change this view: Evidence that the margin gain comes from durable structural causes, such as mix or pricing, and that revenue growth has stabilised at or above 14% for the next reported periods, would make me drop the objection.
